key_insight: Syndrome records alone can be used in classical post-processing to cancel residual logical bias in quantum circuits without prior noise learning or modified quantum experiments.
engineering_relevance: This offers a practical path to more accurate early fault-tolerant quantum computing by reducing logical error bias while avoiding extra calibration overhead and circuit redesign.
method: Use only measured syndrome records after execution
Apply virtual error cancellation in classical post-processing
Pair a fast in-experiment decoder with a stronger offline decoder
evidence_signal: Numerical simulations on a distance-7 rotated surface code show the dual-decoder approach can reduce error with more samples and achieve over three orders of magnitude suppression versus the decoded logical error rate in an experimentally achievable setting.
watch_item: The approach still depends on decoder quality and sample availability, so real hardware performance may be limited by finite statistics and implementation overhead.
paper_title: Measure Now, Mitigate Later: Virtual Error Cancellation for Logical Quantum Circuits
